title: "Recipe: attack the platform, then verify"

**Tool:** mlflow-bypass + mlflow · **Section:** Attack–defence pairs ·
**Level:** hard · **Time:** ~45 min · **Layer/Category:** ATTACK A-7 +
OPS O-1 · **Tags:** pair, attack, mlflow, exp, platform

## Problem

The pairing thesis is Kailash's core idea: deployment + attack in one
declared environment. You suspect an exposed MLflow tracking server
(sensitive-info + platform exploitation: the attack row maps OWASP
LLM02 and LLM10). You want to demonstrate the exploitation against
the lab-default posture, then prove the same declaration hardened
closes the hole — with both sides reproducible, and a standing CI
test asserting the pairing.

## Solution

Kailash ships both ends: the O-1 lab target (`mlflow`, module
packaging, `services.kailash.mlflow` — lab-accurate vulnerable-ish
defaults that are DOCUMENTED, not improvised) and the A-7 exploit
tool (`mlflow-bypass`, exp-classified, manifest-pinned):

```bash
# 1. Stand up the lab target (the OPS module's declared service)
#    kailash.layers.ops.categories.o-01-mlops-ml-engineering.enable = true;
#    services.kailash.mlflow.enable = true;        # + the module's
#    hardened-posture options (see provenance note)
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 2. Open the exp double-key gate for the attack tool
#    (host key + shell key — full walk:
#     ../admin/lab-mode-gating.html)
#      kailash.labMode = true;      # host key, config + rebuild
KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1 mlflow-bypass --help
#    -> the gate passes; the tool's real help prints

# 3. Run the probes as their --help states them, against the
#    lab-default (unauthenticated) target
KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1 mlflow-bypass <args from --help> \
    --target http://127.0.0.1:5000
#    -> the bypass lands: experiment/artifact listing exposed

# 4. Verify: flip the lab target's POSTURE with a configuration
#    change, rebuild
sudo nixos-rebuild switch

# 5. Re-run the SAME probes from the same box (same seed/args)
KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1 mlflow-bypass <same args> --target http://127.0.0.1:5000
#    -> refused / no listing: the declaration change closed the surface
```

What success looks like:

- run A (lab-default posture): the bypass succeeds and the listing is
  asserted — the same assertion the repo's integration test makes
- run B (hardened posture): the same probes fail — a diff of the two
  runs states the surface closed with the configuration change
- the exp gate visibly refused every step 3 shape at any wrong key
  combination along the way
- the standing proof exists without you: the OS repo's
  `integration-mlflow-attack.nix` asserts lab-default MLflow +
  `mlflow-bypass` → listing on every relevant CI run (the pairing
  thesis, executed)

## Discussion

- **Why this pair is the thesis:** the manifest rows mean it —
  `mlflow-bypass` says "pairs with the O-1 lab target", and the O-1
  module ships the platform target as a first-class service. One
  declared environment produces both the finding and the verification;
  no hand-assembled lab whose posture drifts between runs.
- **The attack tool is exp + the LICENCE IS UNKNOWN:** the manifest
  row records `LicenseRef-Unknown` — possession and use in your lab
  is your compliance decision; treat the tool's redistribution as
  unrestricted-by-default until the row's licence is established.
- **ATLAS mapping is the row's record:** the A-7 tool carries
  AML.T0049/T0050 (dataset-verified ids, per the packaging lane),
  the OWASP LLM02/LLM10 mapping sits on both epochs. Cite the row's
  ids in reports; don't re-derive them by memory.
- **Hardened postures are configuration, not folklore:** the exact
  hardened options for the lab target are read from its module and
  documented per release (see provenance note) — flipping the
  posture is a declaration edit plus a rebuild, and the previous
  generation remains one reboot away (see
  [Ride a release without breaking pinned tooling](../admin/updates.html)).
- **Beyond MLflow:** A-7's sister rows (`triton-pwn` etc.) pair the
  same way with their O-2 docker-wrapper targets; the recipe pattern
  is identical — lab target up, gate open, probes run, posture flip,
  same-seed re-run, diff as the evidence.
